journey_description: Two professionals — Omar, a solo weekday regular, and Grace, a thirty-person office coordinator — travel from a trusted colleague’s tip about a signature Dish at the Truck, through solo vetting, the App, and group Catering orders, to opting into the lunch alerts and Catering Newsletter that turn an earned habit into a subscribed, year-round relationship.

rewrites.GOAL-SHAR-0002: Be instantly verifiable at the moment of the tip: location, schedule, and a visible group/Catering path
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0001: Register a credible new lunch option without spending any real decision effort on it — a tip from a colleague I trust means the first try is already vetted
rewrites.GOAL-SHAR-0003: Let the hero Dish prove the quality-to-time promise in a single solo visit
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0004: Answer the only question that matters in one visit: is it worth the minutes — very good brisket in six minutes, not the best brisket in the city
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0005: Figure out what could let me down — how long the line gets, and whether the truck’s even there on a given day
rewrites.GOAL-SHAR-0006: Open a working group and Catering channel with availability and pricing up front
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0009: Know before I leave the desk, every time: open, where, and how long is the line
rewrites.GOAL-GRAC-0009: Get a direct line to the Calgary operator and keep it warm: availability, menu, headcount, dietary
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0011: Find an obvious way to just book them for a proper paid working lunch — the one that beats the same three sad sandwich platters
rewrites.GOAL-SHAR-0009: Convert the earned habit into owned subscriptions: the truck-day alert and the Catering list
rewrites.GOAL-OMAR-0015: Keep turning the morning alert into group runs — two to four colleagues, several times a week, happily
rewrites.GOAL-GRAC-0014: Stop having to remember BorderBlend exists — have them come to me at the right moment of the year with the practical details I actually need
rewrites.GOAL-GRAC-0016: Become the person who sends more business their way, year-round, winter option included
rewrites.NARR-OMAR-0002: Thursday, a rare 90-minute gap, so I go. Reluctantly — a line at 12:40 is a real risk to a 1 o’clock, and I have been the guy who walks in late holding a taco. Once. Not again. Eight people ahead of me; I time it. Eleven minutes to the window, order the smoked brisket taco, and — it’s genuinely good. Actually smoked, not a sauce pretending. Good enough that I registered it, which food rarely does when I’m in work mode. Desk to desk: twenty-two minutes. Eighty percent of a restaurant for twenty percent of the time cost. That ratio, I’ll take.
rewrites.NARR-GRAC-0002: So I take my own lunch hour for this — that’s the rule, non-negotiable, I’ve been burned before. I walk over to the truck by the LRT, stand in the line like a civilian, and order the smoked brisket. And, credit where it’s due: it’s very good. Not sad-tray-of-sandwiches good — actually good, actually smoked. But here’s the thing, I’m not just eating, I’m watching. How fast the line moves. How the two of them handle the rush. And I clock that the brisket sells out — early afternoon, gone. Great problem for them. A flashing warning light for me and my thirty people.
rewrites.NARR-OMAR-0003: I didn’t decide to become a regular. It happened. Two, three times a week now, and increasingly it’s “I’ll grab lunch, what does everyone want” — so I’m carrying four orders in my head, tracking who’s plant-based and who skips the salsa verde. The food has earned its slot; my job is protecting the slot. So I downloaded the app to order ahead — tap from the desk, walk down, one bag waiting. That was the dream. The app didn’t deliver it. Couldn’t tell if the truck was actually open, menu didn’t match the board, no “ready” moment. Used it twice. Closed it. Anyway. Back to walking up and taking my chances — at least when it goes wrong that way, I know exactly how.
rewrites.NARR-GRAC-0003: Right, so now the real work starts. I go back to borderblend.ca looking for the catering page — a “book us” button, anything — and it’s there, but it’s kind of buried, honestly. Built for the one-taco person, not for me booking thirty. I fill out the form, and then the Calgary operator emails back — lovely guy, genuinely — and we sort the actual details over email and one phone call, which I don’t mind, I prefer a human for anything that matters. But there were about four steps before I even knew if my date was available. Meanwhile I’ve sent my form to the team: how many, and who can’t eat what. Friday treat first. Low stakes. That’s deliberate.
rewrites.NARR-OMAR-0004: The stakes went up quietly. It’s not just my lunch now — I’ve vouched for this truck to my team, and I’ve been asked to sort food for a working session: twelve people, client in the room, nobody breaking for an hour. I’d genuinely rather roll up a taco spread than platter number three. So I try to book it and — there’s just no obvious way to do it. Nowhere on the site, nobody to e-mail, no way to say “I would like to give you a defined amount of money for a defined event.” I’m the customer waving money. Meanwhile finance has flagged my fading thermal receipts twice this quarter. I’m not asking them to convince me. I’m already convinced. Make it easy to say yes.
rewrites.QUES-GRAC-0007: The Korean-style chicken, the salsa verde — what’s actually in the sauces? Sesame? Nuts? Shared prep?
rewrites.QUES-GRAC-0010: The plant-based option — is it good enough for my vegetarians, or a token?
rewrites.QUES-OMAR-0017: Does the alert stay accurate — open when it says, where it says, with what it says in stock?
rewrites.QUES-OMAR-0018: Will this list stay pure signal, or does the brand-story stuff start creeping in?
rewrites.PROB-GRAC-0001: The website is clearly built for the person buying one taco on their lunch — nothing on a first look tells me how to order for a group, and I’m the one arriving with real money
rewrites.PROB-GRAC-0005: The menu board tells me “Korean-style chicken taco, delicious” — it does not tell me what’s in the sauce, and I have a colleague with a genuine EpiPen-grade tree-nut allergy, so I cannot guess
rewrites.PROB-GRAC-0009: The catering page is buried on a site built for the one-taco person — I’m arriving waving money and I still have to go hunting for it
rewrites.PROB-OMAR-0014: There’s simply no way I can find to book catering — I’m trying to hand over a large, defined amount of money and I can’t even find where to ask
rewrites.PROB-OMAR-0016: Half these lunches are billable to a project, and without a cost centre or client code on paper the hassle lands on me at month-end
rewrites.PROB-GRAC-0019: One promotional-only e-mail and my trust wobbles — I signed up for the boring, useful version, not a specials flyer, and my unsubscribe finger is famously quick
rewrites.PROB-GRAC-0020: The list only truly pays off if booking comes with it — if I still have to dig up the enquiry form each time, we’re back to everything being on me to initiate
rewrites.TASK-GRAC-0004: Take my own lunch hour for the trial run; order the smoked brisket
rewrites.TASK-GRAC-0005: Watch the truck like a vendor, not just a lunch — how fast the line moves, how they carry themselves, when things sell out, how they speak to customers
rewrites.TASK-OMAR-0011: Try ordering ahead on the app; drop it when walking up turns out to work better
rewrites.TASK-OMAR-0022: Turn the morning alert into group runs — take orders in Slack, walk down once
rewrites.ALTP-GRAC-0001: The website gives me nothing at all for groups, so I quietly file BorderBlend under “nice for someone else’s lunch” and move on to a caterer with proper paperwork
rewrites.ALTP-OMAR-0008: A colleague’s order comes back wrong (salsa verde on the no-salsa one) and I stop volunteering for group runs
rewrites.ALTP-OMAR-0009: I keep the habit solo-only, and the group runs — four orders a trip, several trips a week — never happen for them
rewrites.ALTP-GRAC-0009: The email thread goes quiet for three days mid-planning and I start, quietly, pricing the competitor who has everything spelled out as a fallback
rewrites.ALTP-OMAR-0010: No way to book them turns up in time and the sad sandwich platters win by default — their loss, literally
rewrites.ALTP-GRAC-0010: The allergen answer never firms up, and despite preferring the food I book the competitor with it all spelled out in writing for the client event — not a close call when it’s someone’s airway
rewrites.ALTP-OMAR-0014: The list turns into a newsletter with a brand story; I unsubscribe, keep the lunch habit, and they lose their line to me
rewrites.ALTP-GRAC-0016: The booking-plus-reminder system works flawlessly for a full quarter, and I start trusting them with the client events too — the highest-stakes business I have to give
rewrites.ALTP-GRAC-0017: A referred office manager gets the old chase-the-confirmation experience, and I quietly ease off recommending them until the process catches up with the food
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0001: Description: Be findable at the moment of the tip: an always-current Google Business profile and borderblend.ca location page per Truck showing today’s spot, hours, open/closed status, and the weekly schedule — kept true by an agentic availability monitor fed by operator check-in and POS activity, with no added work for the operator.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0002: Description: A visible group & Catering front door from the very first look: a “Feed your office” path one click from the borderblend.ca homepage, answering the coordinator’s checklist up front — yes we cater, yes we invoice (itemised, GST broken out, your billing name), here’s how headcount works, here’s the Calgary contact, and here’s the winter answer.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0003: Description: Arm the recommender: a lightweight shareable Truck card (link or QR at the Truck) carrying the entire pitch a colleague would give — hero Dish, today’s location and hours, weekly schedule, and one line each for “order ahead” and “we cater offices” — something concrete to forward in Slack instead of pointing at a corner.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0004: Description: Publish the line and the stock: two live data points alongside open/closed status — current line length/estimated wait, and hero Dish stock (“available / running low / sold out”) — fed from POS throughput and a one-tap operator update, propagated by an availability agent to App, web, and the Truck’s Google profile so no channel lies.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0005: Description: Make the window vendor-vet-ready: a physical Catering card at the window (local operator’s name, direct Catering contact, lead times) and an ingredient/allergen sheet — printed and QR-linked — covering every item and sauce at ingredient level, with approved, on-brand language so the answer is consistent Truck to Truck.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0006: Description: Prove consistency to the calculating professional: publish the operational facts a time-boxed professional is silently measuring — peak window (12:15–12:45), typical serve rate (“we move the line at about a minute a person”), and the consistency promise behind the hero Dish (same process, same recipe, every day) — on the Truck card, location page, and App menu.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0007: Description: Answer the pre-departure question every time: Omar’s three data points — open, where exactly, how long is the line — as one glanceable App/web surface that is never wrong. Behind it, an agentic availability monitor: operator check-in opens the day, POS heartbeat confirms activity, geolocation pins the exact corner, and any gap auto-publishes honest “not out today” status to App, web, and maps within minutes.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0008: Description: Group order-ahead that actually deletes the waiting: one order, four labelled items (“Sam — hold the sauce”, “Dana — plant-based”), a menu synced to the Truck’s actual board via POS, a firm “your order is ready” notification, and a labelled bag at a dedicated pickup point — receipts emailed automatically, setting up the Stage-4 expense rails.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0009: Description: Availability-first Catering flow with published per-head pricing: a date-availability checker as step one (“Friday the 14th, Calgary — available”), a published per-head price sheet she can take straight to finance, then menu/headcount/dietary details with the local operator — plus a fast lane that remembers repeat bookers and an operational-response agent that nudges the operator if an enquiry thread goes quiet.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0010: Description: Confirmation-as-standard: every group booking automatically produces a forwardable written confirmation (date, arrival time, duration, Truck, driver’s cell), a ring-fenced stock guarantee (“your 30 covers are reserved and prepped — walk-up demand cannot eat your reserved stock”), and a day-before reminder — assembled by an operational-response agent the moment the operator accepts, with proactive day-of change notification. The same flow gives Omar the discoverable front door for his twelve-person client session.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0011: Description: The allergen dossier: a maintained, versioned allergen and ingredient dossier — every item, every sauce, shared-prep notes — attached automatically to every Catering quote and confirmation, and downloadable from the Catering page. Built once from the brand’s existing recipe documentation, kept current by HQ, so no operator ever has to say “let me check with the kitchen.”
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0012: Description: Business-grade money rails, two tiers on one rail: for Catering, an itemised PDF invoice — GST broken out, billing name, PO reference — issued automatically with delivery, no second ask; for the high-frequency solo/group runner, emailed itemised receipts on every App order with an optional cost-centre/client-code field saved to the account. Repeat bookings reuse billing details so finance sees the same clean paper every time.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0013: Description: The truck-day alert: a subscribable lunch alert — push at ~11:30: “Bay Street Truck open till 2, the hero Dish in stock” — generated automatically by the availability agent from operator check-in, geolocation, and live POS stock, so it is true by construction. Crucially, it also sends the honest negative (“not out today — back tomorrow”), and a group-run shortcut sits inside the notification: tap to open the saved crew order.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0014: Description: The Catering list — “the boring version”: a coordinator-tier subscription that does Grace’s job with her — Catering menu with the allergen dossier attached (forwardable to team and finance in one shot), real availability windows, written confirmations and day-before reminders baked in as standard, and a fast lane for repeat bookings. A proactive seasonal agent initiates at the right moments — “patio season’s starting, here’s how to lock a date,” “November’s coming: here’s the indoor/drop-off option, priced” — and pre-fills recurring dates for one-click confirmation.
rewrites.OPPO-SHAR-0015: Description: Signal-purity governance and the champion loop: govern both subscription channels with a hard editorial rule — operational signal only, enforced with a pre-send check against the brand’s voice model — and rebuild loyalty as operational privilege rather than points theatre: priority pickup on group runs, the repeat-booking fast lane, first access to seasonal Catering dates. Then instrument the champion loop: when Omar recommends the alert or Grace refers another office manager, the referred experience is tracked end-to-end so it matches the one that earned the referral.
